s1.syndrome_frame: Rectal ulcer with a history of radiation therapy
salient_findings: Large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall
key_facts: 57-year-old man
Asymptomatic
History of stage IIIc localized prostate cancer
Completed a course of prostate-directed radiation therapy with a SpaceOAR hydrogel spacer
Mild straining with bowel movements
Occasional passage of mucus
Large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall
Firm margins, friability, and exudate
Biopsies of the lesion were negative for malignancy
Normal appearance of remainder of rectum without radiation-induced changes

shortlist.label: Radiation proctitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of radiation therapy and presence of rectal ulcer

shortlist.label: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall

shortlist.label: Chronic radiation-induced rectal ulcer
shortlist.why_kept: History of radiation therapy and presence of rectal ulcer

shortlist.label: Rectal adenocarcinoma

raw.rationale: The patient's history of prostate-directed radiation therapy and the presence of a large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall with firm margins, friability, and exudate are consistent with radiation proctitis, especially given the recent radiation therapy and the negative biopsy results for malignancy.

rejected.label: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's history of radiation therapy and the acute presentation of the ulcer are more suggestive of radiation proctitis than solitary rectal ulcer syndrome, which is typically associated with chronic straining and rectal prolapse.

rejected.label: Chronic radiation-induced rectal ulcer
rejected.why: While this is a possible diagnosis, the term 'chronic' implies a longer duration of symptoms, which is not clearly indicated in the vignette.

rejected.label: Rectal adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Biopsies of the lesion were negative for malignancy, making rectal adenocarcinoma an unlikely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Prostate cancer metastasis
rejected.why: The negative biopsy results for malignancy and the specific appearance of the ulcer make prostate cancer metastasis an unlikely explanation for the patient's symptoms.
